title: AuraFlow
subtitle: Android Short-Form Media Blocker
summary: Open-source Android app that blocks short-form video feeds while keeping direct messaging usable.
description: An open-source Android app built to block short-form video feeds (Reels, Shorts, Spotlight and similar) across social media platforms while keeping direct messaging and the rest of each app fully functional.
problem: Short-form video feeds are built into apps people still need for messaging. Uninstalling the app or using blunt screen-time limits removes the useful parts along with the distracting ones.
solution: AuraFlow uses Android's Accessibility Service to detect when the user enters a short-form feed inside a supported app and redirects them away, without touching chats, profiles or other screens.
features: Per-app toggles for Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat and other supported platforms
Feed detection through the Accessibility Service view hierarchy
Messaging and non-feed screens remain fully usable
Runs on-device only: no accounts, analytics or network calls
reflections: Working with the Accessibility Service meant designing around UI structures I don't control. When a platform ships an update, detection can break, so the detection rules need to be isolated, easy to update and covered by tests on real view dumps. It also raised a responsibility question: an app with accessibility permissions must be transparent about what it reads and must never collect it.

title: Custom Planner & Scheduler
subtitle: Productivity dashboard
summary: Productivity dashboard with task prioritization, a focus timer, calendar integration and automated Canvas file downloads.
description: A productivity dashboard that brings task prioritization, a built-in focus timer, calendar integration and automated Canvas course-file downloading into one place.
problem: Coursework is spread across Canvas, calendars and to-do lists, so planning a week means checking several tools and manually downloading course files.
solution: A single dashboard that ranks tasks by priority and due date, syncs with the calendar, runs focus sessions and pulls new Canvas files automatically.
features: Task prioritization by urgency and importance
Built-in focus / Pomodoro timer
Calendar integration for deadlines and study blocks
Automated Canvas file downloading and organization
reflections: Building a tool for my own workflow made scope creep easy. Keeping a short list of must-haves and treating everything else as a later iteration kept the project shippable.

title: Automation Chrome Extension
subtitle: Browser workflow automation
summary: Custom browser extension that automates repetitive web actions and streamlines online workflows.
description: A custom Chrome extension built to automate repetitive web actions such as form filling, navigation sequences and page clean-up, streamlining everyday online workflows.
problem: Many everyday web tasks repeat the same clicks and inputs, which wastes time and invites mistakes.
solution: A Manifest V3 extension with content scripts that perform configured actions on matching pages, triggered from the popup or automatically.
features: Configurable automation actions per site
Popup UI for one-click triggers
Content scripts scoped to matching URLs
Settings persisted with chrome.storage
reflections: Working within Manifest V3's permission and service-worker model taught me to request only the permissions an action needs and to design around short-lived background contexts.

title: Media Downloader & File Converter
subtitle: Desktop utility
summary: Utility script and desktop app for downloading online media and batch-converting file formats.
description: A Python utility, available as both a script and a desktop GUI, for downloading online media and batch-converting files between formats automatically.
problem: Downloading media and converting it usually means juggling several single-purpose tools and repeating the same steps for every file.
solution: One app that queues downloads and conversions, applies presets and processes whole folders in a single run.
features: Download queue with progress reporting
Batch conversion between common audio, video and image formats
Reusable output presets
Usable from the command line or the GUI
reflections: Separating the core logic from the interface early let the same code power both the CLI and the GUI, and made each part easier to test.

title: Aura and Artifacts
subtitle: Minecraft gameplay mod
summary: Gameplay mod with an ability skill tree, artifact weapons, custom player animations and modpack integrations.
description: A custom Minecraft gameplay mod featuring an ability skill-tree system, specialized artifact weapons, custom player animations and integrations with popular modpacks.
problem: Vanilla progression is mostly gear-based, which leaves little room for character builds or distinct playstyles.
solution: An Aura skill tree that unlocks abilities as players progress, paired with artifact weapons whose effects scale with the abilities a player has chosen.
features: Ability skill tree with branching specializations
Specialized artifact weapons with unique effects
Custom player animations
Compatibility and integration with modpacks
reflections: Modding a large codebase I didn't write meant reading a lot before writing anything. Keeping balance values in config files made playtesting iterations much faster than recompiling for every change.

title: Custom Roblox Game
subtitle: Multiplayer experience
summary: Fully functional multiplayer Roblox game with custom mechanics, scripting and assets.
description: A fully functional multiplayer Roblox game created with custom gameplay mechanics, scripting and assets.
problem: Building a multiplayer game means keeping gameplay fair and in sync across many clients at once.
solution: Server-authoritative game logic in Lua with client scripts limited to input and presentation, plus custom-built assets and mechanics.
features: Custom gameplay mechanics
Server-authoritative multiplayer scripting
Custom models and assets
Published and playable on Roblox
reflections: My first multiplayer project taught me the client/server split the hard way: anything trusted on the client can be exploited, so the server has to own the game state.

title: Aeris Wildfire Suppression Drone Network
subtitle: APSC 169 design project
summary: Speculative engineering design and technical presentation for an autonomous wildfire suppression drone network.
description: A speculative engineering design project and technical presentation for Aeris, an autonomous network of drones that detects and suppresses wildfires in their early stages.
problem: Wildfires grow fastest in the window before crews and aircraft can reach them, especially in remote terrain where detection is slow.
solution: A distributed drone network that monitors high-risk areas, detects ignitions early and deploys coordinated suppression while relaying data to human responders.
features: System architecture for detection, coordination and suppression
Concept CAD and design rationale
Stakeholder, risk and sustainability analysis
Technical brief and team presentation
reflections: The project pushed me to justify design decisions against stakeholder needs and constraints, not just technical feasibility. Working as a team on a speculative system also showed how much a shared problem definition matters before anyone starts designing.

title: Engineering ePortfolio & Academic Hub
subtitle: This site
summary: Web-based ePortfolio for university engineering reflections, academic goals, documentation and project reports.
description: A web-based ePortfolio that collects university engineering reflections, academic goals, technical documentation and project reports, built with React, Vite and Tailwind and deployed on GitHub Pages.
problem: Academic work, reflections and personal projects usually end up scattered across course platforms, drives and repositories.
solution: One data-driven site where every project lives in a JSON file and can be viewed as either a personal portfolio or a university ePortfolio.
features: Projects stored in a single JSON file
Category filters and a Personal / ePortfolio view toggle
Detail drawer with problem, solution, features and reflections
Deployed automatically to GitHub Pages
reflections: Treating the portfolio as a product rather than a document made me think about the reader: what a recruiter and an instructor each need to find, and how quickly.
